title: video-skill-evals prompt suite
description: A prompt suite is a list of evaluation cases. The canonical on-disk form is an object with metadata plus a 'cases' array; a bare array of cases is also accepted so that a hand-written suite can be the shortest possible file. Loaders should normalise with: cases = suite['cases'] if isinstance(suite, dict) else suite.

version.description: Suite format version. Bump on any breaking shape change.

name.description: Short identifier for the suite, e.g. 'default'.

description.description: Human-readable statement of what this suite is for.

id.description: Stable, filesystem-safe case identifier. Used as the per-case work directory name, so it must never change once results exist for it.

band.description: Difficulty band. Cost and latency budgets are configured per band.

prompt.description: Verbatim user-role prompt handed to the agent under test. It must not mention the rubric, the probes, or this harness: the agent is being graded on what the skill makes it do unprompted.

probes.description: Documented failure modes this case deliberately targets. Every entry names a mode from jaime-troubleshooting.md (or the pitfalls list carried over from Sam's rubric).

notes.description: Why this case exists and what a tripped probe would look like in the artifact. Read by humans triaging a failure, so it must say what to go and look at.

assertions.description: Machine-checkable, deterministically evaluated per-case expectations. Replaces the hand-written per-run job-spec of the prior art. All five keys are required so that a missing expectation is never silently treated as 'anything goes'.

duration_s.description: Inclusive [min, max] finished-runtime window in seconds, measured by ffprobe on the delivered file.

min_scenes.description: Minimum number of distinct scenes/shots the finished video must contain.

aspect_ratio.description: Required display aspect ratio, e.g. '16:9' or '9:16'.

required_concepts.description: Concepts that must be present in the narration script and/or on screen. Checked case-insensitively against the narration text first (deterministic), and only escalated to the judge when the deterministic pass does not find them.

language.description: BCP-47-ish language tag the narration and captions must be in, e.g. 'en'.

probe.description: Closed vocabulary of documented failure modes. Closed on purpose: a typo'd probe name would otherwise silently create a mode nothing reports on.
